gen-dafont-starborn-lora: Lora brings a bookish warmth, with gentle hairline thinning and a welcoming c. Starborn floats above it, dreamy and widely spaced, its dark lowercase stripe leaning heavy where Lora stays light.
gen-dafont-starborn-noto-serif: Starborn drifts in with wide gaps between letters and a dark, dreamy band of lowercase. Noto Serif grounds it with a prominent x-height and a faint thick-thin rhythm, the strongest quality of the two together.
gen-dafont-stencil-fs-sentient: Authoritative and tightly packed, Stencil leans on broad dark verticals while its horizontals shrink to faint hairs. Sentient, a serif, softens that with slightly varied strokes and a more closed, polished look.
gen-dafont-stencilia-lora: Striking in its structure, Stencilia opens spacious gaps at its curve terminals and keeps a compact line. And Lora answers with a taller, moderate lowercase and a slight swell on the bowls, which is where the pair gets its pull.
gen-dafont-stencilia-noto-serif: Structural and striking, Stencilia leads with gaps at its curves. Noto Serif, a serif with a prominent x-height and moderate thick and thin strokes, fills the page beneath it with a steadier, more varied texture.
gen-dafont-stentiga-lora: Lora reads literary and warm, with soft heavy-to-light strokes. Stentiga, spread out and luxurious, has joints that meet without thinning, and that crisp uniform stroke against Lora's soft modulation is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-stentiga-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads universal and bookish, its tall x-height carrying a subtle thick and thin cadence. And Stentiga, with its widely tracked, laser-cut single stroke width, sits above it like a clean, luxurious sign over a handwritten page.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-hind: Refined, glassy and tall in the bowls, Stilu keeps its terminals open. Hind follows with lowercase close to its capitals and a steady, string-straight stroke, so a long passage reads smooth and unhurried.
gen-dafont-true-north-fs-gambetta: True North is stocky and bold, its tall middle band leaving curves open. Gambetta, a serif, lets long text unfold with wide channels into each counter and stroke weight that shifts noticeably but never dramatically.
gen-dafont-true-north-lora: True North is bold and stocky, with a tall middle band and curves left open. Lora, a text serif with moderately weighty stems and no harsh hairlines, gives a softer counterpoint, and body text feels natural a few points smaller than the heading.
